instructions.title: How to use JWT Decoder

steps.title: Paste your JWT token
steps.description: Copy your JWT from an API response, browser DevTools, or Authorization header and paste it into the input. The decoder instantly splits it into header, payload, and signature sections.

steps.title: Inspect the decoded claims
steps.description: Browse the decoded header (algorithm, token type) and payload (user ID, roles, issued-at, expiration) in the structured panel. Timestamps display in both Unix and human-readable format.

steps.title: Track the live expiration countdown
steps.description: The color-coded bar shows exactly how long until the token expires: green (valid), yellow (expiring in less than 5 minutes), red (already expired).

steps.title: Verify the signature (optional)
steps.description: Expand the Verify Signature section, paste your secret (HMAC) or PEM public key (RSA/EC), and click Verify to cryptographically confirm the token is untampered — entirely in your browser, nothing sent to any server.

features: Instant decoding of any JWT into header, payload, and signature
Live expiration countdown with color-coded status — valid, expiring, or expired
In-browser signature verification: HS256, HS384, HS512, RS256, RS384, RS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, PS256
Zero data leakage — no token or key ever leaves your browser
Human-readable timestamps for exp, iat, nbf and all date claims
Header inspection — alg, kid, typ and any custom fields
Works offline after initial page load
useCases: Debug 401 Unauthorized errors by checking if the token has expired or contains wrong claims
Verify a new JWT library produces correctly-signed tokens during development
Inspect ID tokens from OAuth2/OIDC providers — Auth0, Okta, Cognito, Google
Confirm the algorithm in the header matches what your server expects
Validate that sensitive data is not accidentally stored in the JWT payload
Test JWT generation scripts and verify signature correctness with a known secret
Share decoded token content with teammates for debugging without exposing secret keys
proTips: Copy tokens directly from browser DevTools — Network tab, Authorization header
For RS256/ES256, paste only the public key — never share your private key with any online tool
The kid (key ID) field in the header tells you which key from your JWKS endpoint signed the token
Test with a deliberately invalid token first to confirm the verifier correctly rejects it
Monitor the live countdown during load tests to catch short-lived tokens expiring mid-run
troubleshooting: Invalid JWT format — the token must have exactly three dot-separated parts: header.payload.signature
Signature shows INVALID for HS256 — check the secret is the raw string, not base64-encoded
RS256/ES256 verify fails — ensure the public key is in PEM format and includes the BEGIN/END header lines
Claims show unexpected values — the payload is base64url-encoded, not encrypted; anyone with the token can decode it
Signature verification uses the Web Crypto API, available in all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)
